The new volume is empty because adding a JBOD volume moves nothing: the partitions already on data-0 stay there and only some new replicas land on data-1. Strimzi says to use Cruise Control to reassign partitions after adding volumes. Your earlier rebalance ran without rebalanceDisk: true, so it balanced load between brokers only; only a rebalance with rebalanceDisk: true balances the disks within a broker, and Cruise Control does not do inter-broker and intra-broker balancing at the same time.

Use intra-broker disk balancing:

apiVersion: kafka.strimzi.io/v1
kind: KafkaRebalance
metadata:
  name: balance-disks
  namespace: kafka
  labels:
    strimzi.io/cluster: core
spec:
  rebalanceDisk: true
  concurrentIntraBrokerPartitionMovements: 2

Do not give goals with rebalanceDisk: true; Cruise Control configures the intra-broker goals itself, so drop DiskCapacityGoal. Drop concurrentPartitionMovementsPerBroker too: it limits movements between brokers, not between disks. Disk moves are limited by concurrentIntraBrokerPartitionMovements (default 2); raise it carefully if the run is too slow. Approve the proposal after reading it (strimzi.io/rebalance=approve) and wait for Ready. Before and after, check where the partitions live with kafka-log-dirs.sh --describe from a separate helper pod, not inside a broker container. Data stays online during the move. Do not delete pods or PVCs to make room.

value:
Three problems and one risk.

1. API access (the risk). webserver.security.enable: false removes authentication from the Cruise Control REST API for everyone who can reach it. Keep security on and give the UI its own user: put "cc-ui: <password>, USER" in a file in HashLoginService format (USER, because VIEWER only reaches kafka_cluster_state, user_tasks and review_board), create a Secret from it, and reference it under spec.cruiseControl.apiUsers with type: hashLoginService and valueFrom.secretKeyRef.

2. webserver.http.port does nothing. Options with the webserver.http. prefix are managed by Strimzi and cannot be set; the operator ignores them and logs a warning. Point the UI at the default API port.

3. CPU capacity. The description is wrong: when neither brokerCapacity.cpu nor overrides set CPU, Cruise Control takes requests.cpu from the node pool before limits.cpu. It will see 4 and 8 cores, not 8 and 16. For accurate CPU goals, set requests equal to limits in both pools, or set the CPU capacity explicitly (cpu: "8" for all, and an override with cpu: "16" for brokers 6, 7 and 8).

4. Disk. Remove disk: Strimzi generates the disk capacity from the storage itself, so you do not set it.

The network values (1250MB/s, and 3125MB/s for the 25 Gbit/s nodes) are fine.

The pause did not hold because ingest is managed through KafkaConnector resources (strimzi.io/use-connector-resources: "true"): the Cluster Operator reverts changes made directly through the Kafka Connect REST API. The KafkaConnector partner-orders has no spec.state, which means running, so at its next reconciliation the operator resumed the connector.

Task 1 is different because a failed task does not move to PAUSED until it has been restarted; it was FAILED before the pause and stayed FAILED. Read its trace (GET /connectors/partner-orders/status) separately; that fault started at 00:40, before the maintenance.

For Sunday, change the resource itself, and do it in Git, where the pipeline applies it, so that the desired state stays recorded:

spec:
  state: stopped

For a 4-hour window stopped is better than paused: stopping shuts the tasks down and frees their resources, pausing keeps the tasks instantiated. Check that the status shows STOPPED (kubectl get kafkaconnector partner-orders -n data -o yaml, or GET /connectors/partner-orders/status). After the window set spec.state: running (or remove the field) and check that both tasks are RUNNING. Going back is the same change in the other direction.

value:
Don't merge it.

The error is not about the ConfigMap itself. Argo CD applies client-side by default, and client-side apply writes the whole object into the kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration annotation. Annotations are limited to 262144 bytes, and your dashboards are about 410 KB. Server-side apply does not use that annotation. Enable it for just this resource:

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: kafka-grafana-dashboards
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: ServerSideApply=true

(or add ServerSideApply=true to the Application's syncOptions). Then sync again.

Why the PR is dangerous:
- Replace=true makes Argo CD use kubectl replace/create, which can lead to resources being recreated. It also takes precedence over ServerSideApply=true, so it would block the real fix.
- Force=true,Replace=true makes Argo CD sync a KafkaTopic by kubectl delete/create. Each time it deletes a KafkaTopic resource, the Topic Operator deletes the topic in Kafka, with all its data, and the recreated resource gives you an empty topic.

Keep one limit in mind: a ConfigMap cannot exceed 1 MiB, whatever apply method is used. As the dashboards grow towards that, split them over several ConfigMaps.

1. DNS. Your default-deny isolates the pods for egress, and that blocks DNS too, so invoice-writer cannot even resolve prod-kafka-bootstrap.kafka.svc. Add an egress rule to the cluster DNS (UDP and TCP 53 to the DNS pods in kube-system).

Guardrails before opening it up:

1. The templated project. project: '{{.path.basename}}' plus teams creating directories means anyone can create teams/default (or the name of a more permissive project) and deploy under it. Argo CD's rule: if project is not hard-coded, admins must control every source of truth of the generators. So only the platform team creates team directories (protect the top level of the repository), or hard-code the project.

2. Tight team projects from day one, not 'all kinds, all namespaces':

spec:
  sourceRepos: [https://git.example.com/platform/kafka-topics.git]
  destinations:
  - server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: kafka
  clusterResourceWhitelist: []
  namespaceResourceWhitelist:
  - group: kafka.strimzi.io
    kind: KafkaTopic

A project that can deploy into the Argo CD namespace grants admin-level access.

3. Topic collisions: add FailOnSharedResource=true to the template's syncOptions, so an Application fails to sync a KafkaTopic another Application already applied.

4. Topic sizes: a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy on kafkatopics that rejects, for example, more than 24 partitions or replicas other than 3.

5. Capacity: 35 x 40 x 12 x 3 = 50,400 partition replicas, about 8,400 per broker on 6 brokers. Decide what prod can carry and give teams quotas accordingly.

And no team-owned ApplicationSets in the argocd namespace: they can create Applications in any project, so only admins may manage them there.
